clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man with NF1 diagnosed 28 years prior to this presentation was referred to clinic with a recent left apical pneumothorax and a history of recurrent spontaneous pneumothorax (at least 4 episodes affecting both lungs, most recent in 2006, each treated with tube thoracostomy). Clinical diagnosis of NF1 was established based on characteristic features including café-au-lait macules, axillary and groin freckling, multiple neurofibromas and plexiform neurofibromas on face, trunk, and extremities, tongue fibromas, and optic pathway glioma in the right eye, with positive family history (mother and sister with NF1). The diagnosis was confirmed by genetic testing showing a pathogenic NF1 gene variant c.6709C>T; p.Arg2237. Imaging with high-resolution computed tomography revealed bilateral lung bullae and apical cysts, which are recognized pulmonary manifestations of NF1 that predispose to spontaneous pneumothorax. The patient was initially referred with suspicion of Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome due to the recurrent pneumothorax history, but genetic testing confirmed NF1 as the underlying diagnosis.
